 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Borussia Dortmund have taken sole control of first place in the Bundesliga with a gritty 1-0 victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach this afternoon. Felix Nmecha's second-half strike proved to be enough for Niko Kovač's side.
 Looking to pick up where he left off before the international break, Felix Nmecha stung the palms of Daniel Batz. Gladbach's first-choice goalkeeper was forced to tip over a header from the Dortmund midfielder minutes later.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Approaching the half-hour, Gladbach began to threaten. A Joe Scally volley sailed just past the post, while the American wing-back set about creating a chance for Robin Hack. The German winger could only head over the bar.
 Perhaps typical of most Dortmund first-half performances, they showed little in attack. The hosts also had a brief penalty appeal which ultimately didn't go their way. Joane Gadou's handball was deemed unintentional.
 After the break, both Borussen came close to scoring with Hack at one end and Maximilian Beier at the other. Gregor Kobel was called into action nearing the hour, diverting a Shuto Machino pile-driver around the left upright.
 Fábio Silva, deputizing for the injured Guirassy, spurned a wonderful Julian Ryerson cross as Joey Veerman entered the fray. Batz, however, was doing a fine job between the sticks, sponging Kostas Karetsas' near post shot.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Eventually, Dortmund's relentless pursuit was rewarded. Perhaps fortuitously too, as Nmecha fizzed a shot through bodies. Batz, who had been so reliable until then, failed to prevent it from ricocheting into the roof of the net.
 Holding out through injury time, the final whistle brought the biggest cheer of the afternoon for Dortmund. Niko Kovač's side move two points clear of Bayern Munich, while Gladbach stay rooted to the Bundesliga's basement.
